name: upgrade_pydantic_field_regex_to_pattern
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x Field(regex=...) to 2.x Field(pattern=...) - the regex kwarg was REMOVED and raises PydanticUserError immediately at class-definition time under pydantic 2.x; incomplete-fix broken migrates to pattern= but drops the ^...$ anchors, so a string merely CONTAINING three consecutive uppercase letters anywhere wrongly validates
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Item in item.py uses the pydantic 1.x `Field(regex=r"^[A-Z]{3}$")` pattern to require code to be exactly three uppercase letters. The `regex` kwarg was REMOVED in pydantic 2.x - it now raises a PydanticUserError immediately when the class is defined, telling you to use `pattern` instead. Migrate code's Field to use `pattern=` with the SAME regex text (including the ^ and $ anchors - do not drop them). After the fix, a code that merely CONTAINS three uppercase letters somewhere inside a longer or differently-shaped string (e.g. "ABCD" or "XABCX") must still be rejected, not just one that is exactly three uppercase letters.
